in_hebrew.name: לוקא
in_hebrew.meaning: לוּקָא הוּא שֵׁם שֶׁל מְגִילָה בַּתּוֹרָה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: לוּקָא שֵׁם שֶׁל מְגִילָה בַּתּוֹרָה, מִתְאָרֵךְ לְגַמָדִים וְלִפְרָשׂוֹת שֶׁל דְּבָרִים הַמְקוֹרִיִּים בְּקִרְבָּנוֹת הָאֱלֹהִים. הוּא קֶשֶׁר לַעֲמוּדָה וְלִפְרָשָׂה שֶׁל הַמְשׁוֹרֵר בַּכְנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים.

in_greek.name: Λουκάς
in_greek.meaning: Λουκάς ο ευαγγελιστής και συνοδός του Παύλου
in_greek.long_meaning: Λουκάς σημαίνει 'ο φέγγος' ή 'ο λευκός', συνδέεται με την αποστολή του Ευαγγελιστή Λουκά, συγγραφέα του Ευαγγελίου και των Πραξεων των Αποστόλων, που ήταν σύντροφος του Αποστόλου Παύλου και ιατρός.

in_latin.name: Lucas
in_latin.long_meaning: Lucas nomen derivatur a latino 'lux', quod lucem significat. Lucas in Ecclesia primitiva erat sanctus et evangelista, medicus et scriptor Actuum Apostolorum et Evangelii secundum Lucam.

in_english.name: Luka
in_english.meaning: Bringer of light, born at dawn or morning light
in_english.long_meaning: The name Luka is derived from the Latin 'lux', meaning light. It is associated with Saint Luke, the evangelist and companion of Saint Paul, who wrote the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles. Luka symbolizes illumination, knowledge, and spiritual guidance. Historically, the name has been popularized in various Christian cultures, reflecting its biblical and apostolic roots.

data.cultural_impact: The name Luka holds a rich cultural significance due to its illustrious namesake, St. Luke, who was a prominent Early Christian figure. He was a physician by profession, one of the Seven Deacons, and a close associate of St. Paul. St. Luke is known for his authorship of the Gospel of Luke, the Acts of the Apostles, and several Pauline epistles. The name Luka is also popularly associated with St. Luke of Crimea, a 14th-century monk, theologian, and archbishop, who played a crucial role in the spread of Christianity throughout Eastern Europe and Asia.
